prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, demi-statue demi statue portrait, five-material body: real face and neck, one crystal arm, one stone arm, a water-filled glass torso, one glass leg with its own coloured water and contents ending in a sealed tip, and one wooden leg ending in a carved tip. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually finished leg-tips, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her form comes to an end, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Chinese woman in weixun makeup — clear fair skin, a warm rose-red wash blended across the outer corners of both eyes and drifting up toward the temples, the same flush spreading softly across the cheekbones and the bridge of the nose, slightly smudged, dewy highlights, soft brown-pink eyeshadow, large moist eyes with bright real catchlights and a faint glassy shine, moist rose-tinted lips, long black hair loosely tousled with a few strands across the face, a dreamy, half-lidded expression. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a big rose-gold hoop hangs clear of the neck down to the shoulder.

Physique: A colossal heavy chest wider than her shoulders, a waistline that still pulls in sharply, then an enormous belly and colossal wide hips flaring out again, her left arm made of crystal, her right arm made of carved stone, her torso a glass vessel, her left leg a glass vessel ending in a sealed tip, her right leg carved wood ending in a carved tip.

Boundary (skin to material, at the collarbones): a single straight, flat line runs around the base of her neck and across both collarbones, nowhere lower, never reaching her chest — never jagged, never zigzag, a clean straight cut like a cross-section, exactly like a clean slice through a cast-glass sculpture. Real skin above this straight line, the material immediately below it. At that line, the material's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow. The vessel portion is already full of water right up to this same straight collarbone line and no higher.

Left arm (shoulder to hand): solid transparent crystal, solid deep ruby-red cast glass, with slow internal swirls and a few tiny air bubbles, deepest crimson where thickest and pale rose at every thin edge, one continuous carved mass, never hollow, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same crystal. Light passes straight through it; the backdrop is visibly bent inside it.

Right arm (shoulder to hand): carved from ONE solid block of genuine nephrite jade, a rich translucent-edged green stone with soft internal clouding, polished to a smooth waxy sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same stone. No light passes through it — only reflections on its polished surface.

Torso (chest, belly, hips): a sculpted vessel of thick, crystal-clear glass (unmistakably glass: thick, crystal-clear and polished, bright specular reflections, sharp white highlights, tiny trapped bubbles) in the exact shape of her torso, filled completely to the brim with clear deep sapphire-blue water — a distinctly different colour from the water in her left leg below — no hollow space and no air gap anywhere inside it. Small bright fish and slow-drifting green water plants move freely through the whole filled torso, rising up to the collarbone line itself, never crowding. Light passes through; the backdrop is visibly bent inside it.

Left leg (hip to demi-statue tip): a sculpted vessel of the same clear glass (unmistakably glass: thick, crystal-clear and polished, bright specular reflections, sharp white highlights, tiny trapped bubbles), completely filled with clear citrine-gold water — a distinctly different colour from the torso's water above — holding a scattered handful of warm points of firefly-gold light, each caught inside a tiny glass droplet, never crowding, mostly open clear water around each one. A little further below the middle of her thighs, just above where the knee would be, the left leg curves inward and seals shut into its own smooth, rounded, closed tip — the material simply comes to its natural end there.

Right leg (hip to demi-statue tip): carved from ONE solid block of bold bocote wood, a dark chocolate-brown wood marked with bold swirling black tiger-stripe patterns, polished to a hard satin sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque, the grain running unbroken down the leg. A little further below the middle of her thighs, just above where the knee would be, the right leg curves inward and rounds off into its own smooth, satin-polished carved tip — the wood simply reaching its natural end there.

Where each material meets its neighbour (left shoulder, right shoulder, left hip, right hip), the two distinct materials sit flush against each other with a thin, clean seam, deliberate and precise, never jagged or torn — always the finish of a sculpture, each material keeping its own colour, clarity and surface completely separate from the one beside it.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a deep royal blue on one side and a warm golden amber on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, her left hand (crystal) resting on her flared hip, her right arm (stone) held clear of her body, the hand relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so blue light glances off the left half and amber light glances off the right half — passing straight through the crystal arm, the glass torso and the glass leg, while only reflecting off the stone arm and the wooden leg. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
